content:
Apple is adjusting its bug bounty program as it grapples with a flood of "AI slop" security reports. Details below.

Apple Caps Unprocessed Bug Reports

Apple confirmed to the Financial Times that it has "introduced caps and a 30-day cooling-off period in its internal security portal, with users required to submit an application to increase their quota."

The measures, implemented in June, are aimed at addressing an industry-wide surge in bug reports fueled by increasingly powerful large language models that can discover, chain, and exploit vulnerabilities, making it difficult for review teams to keep up with submissions.

Weeks ago, Apple confirmed it was accelerating security updates in response to those AI tools, shipping iOS 26.5.2 and corresponding fixes ahead of schedule—patches originally planned for last week's 26.6 release.

In the security notes for those releases, Apple thanked researchers who used AI tools from OpenAI, Anthropic, Z.ai, and other companies to help uncover multiple vulnerabilities.

One of the thanked teams, Calif.io, said in May that it took just five days using Anthropic's Mythos Preview model to construct a working macOS kernel memory corruption exploit on an M5 chip.

The Financial Times report comes days after GitHub rolled out its own bug bounty tiering system aimed at curbing AI slop while differentiating submissions from verified security researchers.

The Financial Times report tells the story of Bynario, a seven-person cybersecurity startup that has been using recently released AI tools and models to find vulnerabilities; the company submitted five bug reports to Apple this year and eight last year, "one of which was patched in a software update in November," before being blocked from submitting further reports.

Following the Financial Times report, Apple has now reached out to Bynario and is reviewing its findings, including a potential privilege escalation exploit chain that could give an attacker full control of a Mac.

Apple's statement to the Financial Times on the bug bounty changes:

The company added that researchers "can easily request an increased limit at any time, ensuring important reports reach our security team."
